blocks.body: The conventional target is three to six months of essential expenses — not of income — held in an insured, liquid account. Start with a starter fund of $1,000 or one month of expenses so a small surprise does not become new debt, then build to the full target after the employer match and high-interest debt. Size toward the high end, or beyond it, when income is variable, when one earner supports the household, when there are dependents, or when re-employment in your field is slow. If your health plan has a high deductible, plan for its out-of-pocket maximum as well, less whatever your HSA already holds for medical bills.
blocks.plain: The usual target is three to six months of essential costs — not of income — kept in an insured account you can reach quickly. Start with a small fund of $1,000 or one month of costs, so a small surprise doesn't become new debt. Then build to the full target after getting your employer match and paying off high-interest debt. Aim higher, or beyond the range, if your income goes up and down, if one person supports the household, if you have dependents, or if finding a new job in your field takes a long time. If your health plan has a high deductible, also plan for its out-of-pocket maximum (the most you'd pay in a year for in-network care), minus what your HSA (health savings account) already holds for medical bills.

blocks.body: Health coverage is a Tier-1 item in the plan for a reason: one uninsured hospital stay can turn a stable budget into unpayable debt. ACA-compliant plans cap in-network out-of-pocket spending each year (2026 cap: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family); that cap, not the premium, is the number your cash reserves should aim to cover. If that is out of reach, check whether you qualify for Medicaid, whose rules vary by state, or for cost-sharing reductions, which lower the cap on a Marketplace silver plan. Nonprofit hospitals must have a written financial assistance policy; ask for it before paying a large bill.
blocks.plain: Health coverage is a Tier-1 (top-priority) step for a reason: one hospital stay without insurance can turn a steady budget into debt you can't pay. ACA-compliant plans limit what you pay in-network each year (2026 limit: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family). That limit, not the premium, is the amount your savings should aim to cover. If that is out of reach, check whether you qualify for Medicaid (the rules differ by state) or for cost-sharing reductions, which lower the limit on a Marketplace silver plan. Nonprofit hospitals must have a written financial assistance policy. Ask for it before you pay a large bill.

blocks.body: Social Security says more than 1 in 4 people who are 20 will become disabled before reaching retirement age, and an earner's future income is usually their largest asset. Most private-sector workers have no group long-term disability plan. Where there is one, it commonly replaces about 60% of base salary up to a monthly cap; if your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxable, which lowers the real replacement rate. The policy features that decide whether a claim pays — own-occupation versus any-occupation definition, the elimination period, the benefit period — matter as much as the percentage. Social Security disability pays only for severe, long-lasting conditions, and only after a waiting period; some states run paid leave or temporary disability programs.
blocks.plain: Social Security says more than 1 in 4 people who are 20 will become disabled before reaching retirement age, and your future pay is usually your biggest asset. Most workers at private employers have no group long-term disability plan. Where there is one, it often replaces about 60% of base pay, up to a monthly cap. If your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxed, so you really get less. The policy details that decide whether a claim pays — whether "disabled" means unable to do your own job or any job, how long you wait before benefits start, how long benefits last — matter as much as the percentage. Social Security disability pays only for serious, long-lasting conditions, and only after a waiting period. Some states run paid leave or temporary disability programs.

blocks.body: Life insurance replaces income for people who depend on it, whether children or a spouse; with no one relying on your income, or on you to repay a loan they co-signed for you, it is rarely needed. The common heuristic for a primary earner with dependents is 10–12 times annual income; the DIME method (debt + income for the years needed + mortgage + education) gives a household-specific number. Subtract savings and coverage you already have from either figure, and ask whether employer group life would continue if you left the job. Term coverage is the default for this job; whole-life policies bundle insurance with a low-return savings component.
blocks.plain: Life insurance replaces income for people who rely on it, such as children or a spouse. Subtract the savings and life insurance you already have from either number, and ask whether life insurance from your job would continue if you left. Term insurance is the standard choice for this job. Whole-life policies bundle insurance with a savings part that earns little.

blocks.body: State minimum liability limits are set low and can leave your savings exposed after a serious accident. Consumer guidance commonly suggests at least $100,000 per person, $300,000 per accident and $100,000 property damage. Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage protects you: it pays for your own injuries when the at-fault driver has no insurance or too little, and what insurers must offer, and at what limits, depends on your state.

blocks.body: An umbrella policy adds liability coverage on top of auto and homeowners policies, and carriers usually require higher limits on those policies first. Industry pricing surveys put $1 million at roughly $200–400 a year. Size it to what a lawsuit could actually reach, not to net worth alone: employer retirement plans covered by ERISA are generally shielded from creditors, but a judgment can be collected from future wages within federal limits, so a high earner with little saved is still exposed.
blocks.plain: An umbrella policy adds liability coverage on top of your auto and home policies, and insurers usually require higher limits on those policies first. Industry price surveys put $1 million at roughly $200–400 a year. Choose the amount based on what a lawsuit could actually take, not just your net worth. Workplace retirement plans covered by ERISA (a federal law) are generally protected from people you owe, but a court judgment can be collected from your future pay, within federal limits. So someone who earns a lot but has little saved can still be at risk.

blocks.body: Beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance pass those assets directly and generally override a will, so they are the first thing to check. Bank and brokerage accounts can name a payable-on-death or transfer-on-death beneficiary, who receives the account directly at death. A will directs everything else and is where parents name a guardian for minor children; without one, state intestacy law decides. A durable financial power of attorney lets someone you choose manage your finances if you cannot; without one, a family may need a court-appointed guardian or conservator. A healthcare directive (living will plus a healthcare proxy) records your medical wishes and who decides, and a HIPAA authorization lets named people get your medical information. Once a child is a legal adult, a parent no longer speaks for them by default on medical matters; a young adult can sign their own power of attorney, healthcare directive and HIPAA authorization. Each is governed by state law.
blocks.plain: Beneficiary forms on retirement accounts and life insurance send that money straight to the people named, and they usually win over a will — so check them first. Bank and brokerage accounts can name a payable-on-death or transfer-on-death beneficiary, who gets the account directly when you die. A will covers everything else, and it is where parents name a guardian for young children; without one, your state's law decides who gets what. A durable financial power of attorney lets a person you choose handle your money if you can't; without one, your family may need a court to appoint someone. A healthcare directive (a living will plus a healthcare proxy) records the care you want and who decides for you, and a HIPAA authorization lets people you name get your medical information. Once your child is a legal adult, you no longer speak for them by default on medical matters. A young adult can sign their own power of attorney, healthcare directive and HIPAA authorization. State law governs each of these.

blocks.body: A security freeze stops new credit being opened in your name and is free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion; it does not affect your credit score, and you can lift it temporarily when you apply for credit. You can pull your own reports free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov builds the recovery plan, and reporting unauthorized electronic transfers to your bank quickly limits your liability. An IRS Identity Protection PIN stops someone else from filing a tax return with your Social Security number; anyone who can verify their identity can get one, including for dependents. A parent can also freeze the credit file of a child under 16.
blocks.plain: A security freeze stops anyone from opening new credit in your name. It's free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, it doesn't change your credit score, and you can lift it for a while when you apply for credit. You can check your own credit reports for free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov makes a recovery plan for you, and telling your bank quickly about electronic transfers you didn't make limits how much you can lose. An IRS Identity Protection PIN stops someone else from filing a tax return using your Social Security number. Anyone who can prove who they are can get one, including for their dependents. A parent can also freeze the credit of a child under 16.

new_claims.claim: Most private-industry workers have no access to an employer long-term disability plan; most group LTD plans replace a fixed percentage of earnings (median 60 percent) subject to a maximum amount payable
new_claims.source: BLS National Compensation Survey: Employee Benefits in the United States, March 2026 (news release USDL-26-1534); BLS Beyond the Numbers vol. 4 no. 4 (Feb 2015)
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: BLS release 2026-09-25 ('37 percent had access to long-term disability plans', private industry); BLS BTN ('The median amount covered by long-term plans is 60 percent of annual earnings. Most long-term plans (88 percent) have a maximum amount payable'). Provision data are March 2014. Persona pass findings ADV-50, CFP-50. Type set to GUIDANCE to fit this file's schema; the audit's own vocabulary would call it EMPIRICAL (owner's choice). BLS BTN also gives the median maximum payout in 2014 as $8,000 per month, which supports 'monthly cap'.

new_claims.claim: Social Security disability requires an impairment preventing substantial gainful activity expected to last at least 12 months or end in death, and benefits begin after a waiting period; no temporary or partial benefits
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 42 U.S.C. §423(d)(1)(A) ('inability to engage in any substantial gainful activity ... not less than 12 months'); §423(a)(1) ('the first month after his waiting period'); SSA facts page ('Social Security doesn't provide temporary or partial disability benefits'). Persona pass finding ADV-50.

new_claims.claim: There is no federal paid family and medical leave for private-sector workers, but some states run their own paid leave programs, and one state (Hawaii) a paid temporary disability program
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: DOL ('some states have their own paid leave programs and requirements'; 'Hawaii has a law providing paid temporary disability leave'). Text says 'some states', no count. Persona pass finding ADV-50.

new_claims.claim: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage pays for the policyholder's own injuries when the at-fault driver has no or too little insurance; whether insurers must offer it, and its limits, are set by state law
new_claims.source: Texas Department of Insurance 'Auto insurance guide'; Ohio Department of Insurance 'Automobile Insurance Guide'
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary sources (state agencies, used for the state-variation point): TDI ('pays if you're hit by someone who didn't have insurance or didn't have enough ... Insurance companies must offer you this coverage'); Ohio DOI (UM/UIM 'is an optional coverage'; 'Insurers will not allow you to buy more coverage for UM than you buy for liability coverage', https://insurance.ohio.gov/consumers/automobile/automobile-insurance-guide). Persona pass findings ADV-51, CFP-52.

new_claims.claim: Benefits under ERISA-covered pension plans (including 401(k) plans) may not be assigned or alienated, which generally shields them from creditors
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 29 U.S.C. §1056(d)(1) ('Each pension plan shall provide that benefits provided under the plan may not be assigned or alienated.'). Exceptions (QDROs, federal tax levies) exist; IRAs are not covered by this section. Persona pass finding ADV-52.

new_claims.claim: Ordinary wage garnishment is capped by federal law (generally 25 percent of disposable earnings, or less), so a judgment can reach future wages within federal limits
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 15 U.S.C. §1673(a) (garnishment 'may not exceed (1) 25 per centum of his disposable earnings for that week, or (2) ... whichever is less'). Text says 'within federal limits'; states may cap lower. Persona pass finding CFP-53.

new_claims.claim: Payable-on-death bank accounts and transfer-on-death securities registrations pass the account to the named beneficiary at death without probate; TOD registration is governed by state law
new_claims.source: FDIC 'Your Insured Deposits'; SEC Investor.gov 'Transferring Assets'
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary sources: FDIC ('payable on death ... directing the bank to transfer the funds in the account to one or more named beneficiaries upon the owner's death'); Investor.gov ('pass the securities you own directly to another person or entity upon your death without having to go through probate'; 'State law ... governs', https://www.investor.gov/additional-resources/information/seniors/transferring-assets). Persona pass finding CFP-54.

new_claims.claim: Under the HIPAA Privacy Rule a parent is usually the personal representative of a minor child; for an adult, the personal representative is a person with legal authority to make health decisions for them, such as a healthcare power of attorney
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: HHS ('such as is usually the case with a parent with respect to a minor child'; adult: 'A person with legal authority to make health care decisions on behalf of the individual'). Age of majority is state law, so the text says 'legal adult', not 18. Persona pass finding CFP-54.

new_claims.claim: An IRS Identity Protection PIN prevents someone else from filing a tax return using your SSN or ITIN; anyone who can verify their identity may enroll, and parents may request one for dependents
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: IRS ('prevents someone else from filing a tax return using your Social Security number'; 'Anyone who has an SSN or ... ITIN and is able to verify his/her identity is eligible'; 'Parents and legal guardians can also request an IP PIN for dependents'). The page also announces the online system is offline Nov. 16, 2026 to mid-January 2027. Persona pass finding CFP-55.

new_claims.claim: A parent or other representative can have a free security freeze placed for a protected consumer, defined as a person under 16 (or an incapacitated person under guardianship)
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 15 U.S.C. §1681c-1(j)(1)(B) ('under the age of 16 years at the time a request ... is made') and (j)(2) ('shall, free of charge, place the security freeze'). Persona pass finding CFP-55.

new_claims.claim: A cosigner must repay the debt if the borrower does not, so someone who co-signed your loan relies on you to repay it
new_claims.source: 16 CFR §444.3(c) (FTC Credit Practices Rule, Notice to Cosigner); 15 U.S.C. §1650(g)(2) and note
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 16 CFR 444.3(c) ('If the borrower doesn't pay the debt, you will have to.'). Exception: 15 U.S.C. 1650(g)(2) releases a cosigner on the student borrower's death for private education loans entered into on or after 180 days after May 24, 2018. Persona pass finding CFP-51.
